decisions.reason: Changing the spout geometry to preserve beverage consistency does not alter the existing leak-prevention requirements.
The requested spout geometry change does not modify the established valve mechanism, no-drip behavior, or controlled-flow criterion.
The source does not change the requirement that the spout be removable or easy to clean and flush.
The source concerns downstream spout geometry and froth preservation, not bowl capacity or form.
The existing requirement for high-quality mixing and consistent foam remains unchanged; the source adds a spout-specific preservation constraint rather than changing the mixing result.
The spout modification does not affect the machine name or retained placard wording.
The source does not change whisk size, bowl compatibility, or suitability for fine matcha powder.
The requested spout geometry does not alter the bowl removal or rapid-swapping behavior.
The source addresses consistency and froth loss through the spout and does not modify the splash-control target during mixing.
The design change may inform later component selection, but it does not change the requirement to produce component selections and a BOM.
The spout-specific design constraint does not rescind or modify the general V1 priority for a simple, rapidly built, off-the-shelf approach.
The source does not change the established beige primary color or green accents.
